habit.lifeForm.basis: RHS record of this cultivar: "A large, twining, deciduous climber". Bean, of the species: "A twining shrub scrambling in the wild over bushes and hedgerows".

habit.vigour.basis: Bean's supplement, of this cultivar: found in Warwickshire about 1960, "exceptionally vigorous".

habit.heightM.basis: RHS record of this cultivar: ultimate height 4 to 8 metres, reached in 5 to 10 years. A height band, not a route length.

habit.spreadM.basis: RHS record of this cultivar: ultimate spread 1 to 1.5 metres.

stem.twiningHandedness.basis: As in taxon.json: climbs clockwise seen from above (Wildlife Trusts), a left-handed helix. First Nature also calls it a clockwise climber. No peer-reviewed species-level source was retrieved.

stem.thickestSupportTwinedMm.basis: Of the species. Darwin, The Movements and Habits of Climbing Plants (1875): the honeysuckle "which I have observed twining up a young beech-tree nearly 4 1/2 inches in diameter". One support it did hold, not a measured limit.

stem.young.basis: Of the species. Bean: young stems hollow, "downy or glabrous".

value: purplish where the sun reaches it
stem.youngColour.basis: Of the species. Flora of New Zealand, vol. IV (Webb, Sykes and Garnock-Jones 1988): stems glabrous except towards the inflorescence, more or less purplish where exposed to direct sun. The US plant patent of the similar cultivar 'Scentsation' gives the young stem as green (RHS 143A).

stem.matureColour.basis: Of the species. University of Connecticut plant database: "twining, thin stems, tan colored, glabrous".

stem.oldBark.value: grey-brown, fibrous, peeling in long strips
stem.oldBark.basis: No flora read describes the old bark of this species. Dormice strip honeysuckle bark for their nests (Woodland Trust), which fits a bark that comes away in long fibrous strips; drawn so from that, and not from a description.

leaf.arrangement.value: opposite, each pair at right angles to the next
leaf.arrangement.basis: Of the species. BSBI account of the species in Fermanagh: leaves simple, entire, without stipules, "borne in opposite pairs, each pair at right angles to the next".

leaf.division.basis: Of the species. BSBI account: leaves simple.

leaf.shape.basis: Of the species. Bean: "Leaves ovate, oval, or obovate". The RHS record of this cultivar says oval.

leaf.base.basis: Of the species. Bean: "more or less tapered at the base".

leaf.tip.basis: Of the species. Bean: "mostly pointed, sometimes blunt".

leaf.margin.basis: Of the species. Flora of New Zealand: lamina glabrous, entire. The oak-lobed leaf is f. quercina (Bean), not this plant.

leaf.lengthM.basis: Of the species. Bean: leaves "1 1/2 to 2 1/2 in. long", in metres. The growth model's organs.leafLengthM is the same figure. The Flora of the Burren gives 3 to 7 cm, the Flora of New Zealand 3 to 9 cm.

leaf.widthM.basis: Of the species. Bean: leaves "1 to 1 1/2 in. wide", in metres.

leaf.stalk.value: lower pairs stalked, uppermost almost or quite stalkless, never joined round the stem
leaf.stalk.basis: Of the species. Bean: "lower pairs of leaves stalked, uppermost ones almost or quite stalkless, but never united as in L. caprifolium".

leaf.stalkLengthM.basis: Bean says the lower pairs are stalked and gives no length; the Flora of New Zealand says subsessile or very shortly petiolate; the US plant patent of the similar cultivar 'Scentsation' gives 1 to 1.5 mm. Up to 6 mm is assumed for the stalked leaves of the long shoots.

leaf.colourAbove.basis: RHS record of this cultivar: "oval, dark green leaves that are whitish beneath". A nursery (Ashridge) calls them mid-green.

leaf.colourBeneath.basis: RHS record of this cultivar: leaves "whitish beneath". Bean, of the species: "rather glaucous beneath". The viewer's leaf program gives a leaf one colour on both faces, so this is recorded and not drawn.

leaf.surface.basis: Of the species. Bean: "slightly downy or glabrous". A soft, dull leaf, not a leathery one.

leaf.youngColour.basis: Of the species. BSBI account, after Lang (1987): new leaves open in December and January "from bluish-green buds".

leaf.autumnColour.value: none: the leaves drop while still green
leaf.autumnColour.basis: Of the species. University of Connecticut plant database: "No fall color. Leaves drop while still green". The model lets a leaf dull and yellow a little before it goes.

leaf.belowHead.value: small, nearly circular, the pair free
leaf.belowHead.basis: Of the species. Flora of New Zealand: the uppermost leaves just below the inflorescence are small and suborbicular, sometimes clasping; the pair below the peduncle is free. This is what tells the species from L. caprifolium, whose upper pairs are joined into a cup.

inflorescence.type.value: terminal stalked head of close whorls
inflorescence.type.basis: Of the species. Bean: flowers "in a series of close whorls at the end of the shoot, forming a terminal stalked inflorescence". The RHS record of this cultivar: "in terminal clusters".

inflorescence.flowerCount.basis: Of the species. BSBI account: "umbel-like clusters or whorls of 6-15". The Flora of New Zealand: a head "of up to 20", sometimes with a smaller whorl below. The US plant patent of the similar cultivar 'Scentsation' counts 23 to 25. No count for this cultivar was found.

inflorescence.stalkLengthM.basis: Of the species. Flora of New Zealand: peduncles about 1 to 50 mm long. The patent of 'Scentsation' gives 15 to 20 mm.

inflorescence.widthM.basis: The width of a head across the tips of opposite flowers. This is what the growth model's organs.racemeLengthM measures for this plant, and what the flower model's authored size is. Worked out from the flower: 40 to 50 mm long, standing out all round the end of the stalk. The patent of 'Scentsation' gives an umbel 100 to 120 mm across.

inflorescence.openingOrder.value: the outer whorl first, the buds of the middle standing erect until their turn
inflorescence.openingOrder.basis: No source read gives the order. The BSBI account says only that fresh flowers of the cluster open on later evenings. Drawn as the plant is commonly seen, with open flowers round erect buds.

flower.lengthM.basis: Of the species. BSBI account (after Sell and Murrell 2006): flowers 40 to 50 mm long. Bean: corolla "1 1/2 to 2 in. long". The Flora of New Zealand gives 2.5 to 3.5 cm for plants naturalised there. NC State calls the flowers of this cultivar large.

flower.shape.value: a slender tapering tube opening into two lips, the upper of four lobes, the lower single
flower.shape.basis: Of the species. BSBI account: corolla "a long, slender, funnel-shaped tube, two-lipped: the upper lip has four lobes and the lower lip is solitary". Bean: "two-lipped, the tube slender, tapering". The Flora of New Zealand: lobes becoming reflexed.

flower.upperLipLobes.basis: Of the species. BSBI account: "the upper lip has four lobes".

flower.stamenCount.basis: Of the species. BSBI account: "Five stamens; one style and one stigma". The Flora of New Zealand: stamens exserted, style often long-exserted.

flower.tubeShareOfLength.basis: How much of the flower's length is tube. No flora read gives it. The patent of 'Scentsation' has a tube of 22 to 25 mm in a flower of 30 to 38 mm with lips of 20 mm and more; a little over half is assumed for this cultivar.

flower.upperLipWidthM.basis: Not of this cultivar: the patent of 'Scentsation', which it names as the most similar variety, gives an upper lip 12 to 15 mm wide and a lower lip about 5 mm wide.

flower.lowerLipWidthM.basis: Not of this cultivar: see flower.upperLipWidthM.

flower.tubeWidthM.basis: Not of this cultivar: the patent of 'Scentsation' gives the flower about 2 mm wide at its base and the tube about 3 mm wide.

flower.stamenLengthM.basis: Not of this cultivar: the patent of 'Scentsation' gives stamens 25 to 30 mm long, borne on the tube, and a style about 55 mm long.

flower.styleLengthM.basis: Not of this cultivar: see flower.stamenLengthM. Scaled in the model to the length of this plant's flower.

flower.budLengthM.basis: Not of this cultivar: the patent of 'Scentsation' describes the bud as tubular, inflated and curved, up to 35 mm long and 8 mm wide.

flower.colourOpening.basis: RHS record of this cultivar: "Fragrant white flowers in terminal clusters fade to buff-yellow". Bean's supplement: they open pale whitish-cream.

flower.colourAged.basis: RHS record of this cultivar: the white flowers "fade to buff-yellow". Bean's supplement: they darken to yellow. In the species a flower is yellow from its second evening (BSBI account, after Knight 1996).

flower.redFlush.basis: Bean's supplement, of this cultivar: the flowers have no red. The wild plant is "yellowish white and red in varying proportions".

flower.colourSpent.basis: Of the species. BSBI account: after fertilisation the corolla turns dirty orange-brown and loses its scent. Not drawn: a flower in the model drops as it is.

flower.posture.value: erect in bud, level when open, the style curving down below the anthers
flower.posture.basis: Of the species. BSBI account, after Knight (1996): buds erect in the evening; on opening "the corolla then turns from vertical to horizontal" and the style curves down past the lower lip and below the anthers.

flower.surfaceOutside.basis: Of the species. Bean: the tube "glandular-downy outside".

flower.calyxLobeLengthM.basis: Of the species. Flora of New Zealand: calyx lobes 1 to 2 mm, triangular-ovate, densely glandular; bracteoles 2 to 4 mm, shorter than the ovaries.

flower.scent.basis: RHS record of this cultivar: fragrant flowers. Of the species (BSBI account): the scent is strong from the evening the flower opens and faint by day.

fruit.type.basis: RHS record of this cultivar: the flowers are "followed by red berries".

fruit.berryDiameterM.basis: Of the species. BSBI account: berries 8 mm in diameter, dark red, globose. The University of Connecticut plant database gives a quarter of an inch.

fruit.arrangement.basis: Of the species. BSBI account: berries globose and stalkless, in tight clusters.

fruit.colourRipe.basis: RHS record of this cultivar: "red berries". Of the species: dark red (BSBI account), glossy (RHS record of the species).

fruit.colourUnripe.basis: No source read gives the colour of the unripe berry. Green, passing through orange to red, is assumed.

fruit.berriesPerCluster.basis: No count was found. A head has 6 to 20 flowers (inflorescence.flowerCount) and not every one sets; three to twelve berries to a cluster is assumed.

fruit.clusterWidthM.basis: The width of a cluster of berries: what the growth model's fruit.lengthM measures for this plant, and the fruit model's authored size. Worked out from the berry (8 mm) and a cluster about three berries across, not measured.

fruit.seedCount.basis: Of the species. BSBI account, after Lang (1987): each berry holds five or six yellow seeds, 4.0 by 2.5 mm.
